articleSummary: On 7 June 2026, Thailand's Interior Ministry Permanent Secretary ordered all 76 provincial governors to implement a three-pronged Ebola virus disease (EVD) prevention plan under the Communicable Diseases Act, following WHO reports of an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of Uganda. The outbreak involves Bundibugyo virus and has been declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). articleHeadline: कांगो में इबोला के मामले 500 पार, अब तक 91 लोगों की मौत | Ebola Cases Cross 500 In Dr Congo Including 91 Deaths
articleSummary: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak has exceeded 500 cases with 91 deaths as of June 6, per the health ministry. Recoveries are 12; 117 suspected cases and 283 people in isolation or hospital. No vaccine or specific treatment exists for the Bundibugyo strain, hindering control efforts. Response challenges include weak contact tracing (about 50.3% follow-up vs. a 95% target), community resistance to post‑mortem testing, and limited capacity in standard Ebola Treatment Centers. Shortages of infection prevention supplies and funding, plus strained laboratory capacity, contribute to delays, with many test results pending. The impact spans several affected provinces in the DR Congo, stressing the health system as authorities work to bolster surveillance, diagnostics, and care while awaiting potential therapies or vaccines.

locations: Ho Chi Minh City; Ho Chi Minh City; Socialist Republic of Vietnam
articleHeadlineTranslated: Warning: Risk of a large-scale dengue fever outbreak.
articleHeadline: Cảnh báo nguy cơ dịch sốt xuất huyết bùng phát trên diện rộng
articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City faces a high risk of a large-scale dengue fever outbreak in 2026, according to the city’s Center for Disease Control (HCDC). As of May 31, 2026, there have been 17,718 dengue cases citywide, up roughly 65% compared with the same period in 2025, with activity across all 168 wards/communes. Four dengue-related deaths have occurred this year. The city notes that outbreak cycles are shortening; after 2016, 2019, and 2022, the gap to the next large outbreak has shrunk to about 3–4 years, suggesting a southern Vietnam-wide outbreak in 2026. More than half of cases occur in people aged 15 and older, particularly those 16–30, who are more mobile in crowded environments and may neglect preventive measures. Delayed or self-managed treatment has led to severe dengue and organ failure, while treatment costs for critical cases can range from 120 million to 720 million VND.

locations: São Paulo; Santa Catarina; São Paulo; Federative Republic of Brazil
articleHeadlineTranslated: Presence of antibiotic-resistant superbugs in fish and seafood is growing.
articleHeadline: Presença de superbactérias resistentes a antibióticos em pescados e frutos do mar cresce
articleSummary: Fresh oysters sold in São Paulo and Santa Catarina carried Citrobacter telavivensis for the first time in Brazilian foods, detected in a 2025 study by USP and the São Paulo Institute of Fisheries, along with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli resistant to last-generation antibiotics. Despite passing routine sanitary checks, the findings expose a gap in HACCP/APPCC/GMP protocols which do not screen for antimicrobial resistance. Oysters, as filter feeders, reflect environmental contamination; 35% of samples exceeded arsenic limits set by Anvisa, illustrating co-selection of metal and antibiotic resistance. Globally, WHO’s 2025 GLASS report records about 1 in 6 bacterial infections are resistant, and the May 2025 Global Action Plan projects up to 39 million deaths annually by 2050 if not addressed. Brazil’s 2023 second phase of the National AMR Action Plan pushes seafood surveillance and stronger food safety protocols.
